block.google_calendar.model.title: Google Calendar
block.google_calendar.model.description: List, create, update and watch Google Calendar events.
block.google_calendar.security_hint: The OAuth grant stays in the wallet. Nothing is created, changed or deleted until Allow changes or Allow deletion is enabled.
block.google_calendar.apply_hint: Changes remain local until Apply. Restart a loaded Run to use new settings.
block.google_calendar.invalid_number: Check the numeric value and its limits.
block.google_calendar.help_enabled: Off by default. While off, no request reaches Google and the wallet is never read.
block.google_calendar.help_secret_ref: Wallet reference holding an access token, or JSON with client_id, client_secret and refresh_token. Never the token itself.
block.google_calendar.help_calendar_id: Calendar read by default, changed by create, update and delete, and watched. primary is the account's main calendar; otherwise the ID from the calendar settings.
block.google_calendar.help_operation: Used when a request gives no operation. create_event and update_event need Allow changes; delete_event needs Allow deletion.
block.google_calendar.help_allowed_opera: JSON array among ["list_calendars", "list_events", "get_event", "free_busy", "watch", "create_event", "update_event", "delete_event"]. The default operation is always allowed.
block.google_calendar.help_default_time_: IANA time zone for request times without an offset and for date-only windows. Empty: such times must carry an offset or a request time_zone.
block.google_calendar.help_single_events: On: list_events returns each occurrence of a recurring event. Off: one item per series. A request may choose with single_events.
block.google_calendar.help_list_limit: Upper bound for one list_events or list_calendars; a request limit can only lower it.
block.google_calendar.help_allow_writes: Off by default. Required for create_event and update_event.
block.google_calendar.help_allow_delete: Off by default. Required for delete_event. A deleted event is cancelled for every guest.
block.google_calendar.help_send_updates: Emails Google sends to guests for a change. none by default; a request can only choose fewer notifications.
block.google_calendar.label_allow_reques: Let a request choose the calendar of a change
block.google_calendar.help_allow_request: Off: changes always go to Calendar ID. On: a request may give another calendar_id the account can edit.
block.google_calendar.label_watch_enable: Watch the calendar in Active Runtime
block.google_calendar.help_watch_enabled: Polls Calendar ID while a Run is active and publishes created, updated and cancelled events on changed. One Shot polls only on a watch request.
block.google_calendar.help_watch_interva: Time between two polls, at least 60 seconds. Requested polls of this node also respect the 60-second minimum.
block.google_calendar.help_watch_max_cha: Changes published by one poll; the others wait for the next poll in order.
block.google_calendar.label_emit_existin: Report upcoming events at the first poll
block.google_calendar.help_emit_existing: Off: the first poll only records the current position. On: it also reports up to 100 upcoming events once, as existing.
block.google_calendar.help_page_size: Items requested per Google page (calendar lists use at most 250). A page is never cut, so next_page_token resumes exactly.
block.google_calendar.help_max_pages: Google pages read by one listing or one poll; a listing then returns next_page_token, a poll resumes at the next poll.
block.google_calendar.help_timeout_sec: Total time for one request or one poll, token exchange, pages and retries included.
block.google_calendar.help_max_retries: Reads retry after HTTP 429, a rate-limit 403, 5xx or a lost connection; changes only after a rate limit.
block.google_calendar.help_max_retry_wai: A Retry-After above this value returns rate_limited instead of waiting.
block.google_calendar.help_max_request_b: Bound for the incoming request and for each JSON body sent to Google.
block.google_calendar.help_max_response_: Larger JSON responses from Google are refused as protocol errors.
block.google_calendar.help_api_base_url: Keep https://www.googleapis.com. Another origin receives the access token; plain HTTP only for a loopback test host.
block.google_calendar.help_oauth_base_ur: Keep https://oauth2.googleapis.com. Used only with a refresh-token grant; plain HTTP only for a loopback test host.
block.google_calendar.help_ca_file: Optional absolute PEM file for a privately signed HTTPS origin. TLS verification cannot be disabled.
